transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Liam (Head of Platform), Priya (SRE), Carlos (Procurement)

Auto-generated summary: quick check-in about renewal and expansion, some details missing in recording.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, so we'll go through the proposed amendment, the EU edge provisioning path, and Omar will cover the ops checklist. Quick round-robin intros?

[00:14] Liam (Skybridge): Hey all, Liam here, just to confirm timing we're hoping to have the contract signed before end of Q4, ideally earlier if procurement moves. We also want to ramp EU capacity for our last-mile routing team, so that's the heavy ask.

[00:28] Priya (Skybridge): Priya — SRE. We'll be responsible for the on-prem edge nodes, and our main concerns are network peering, KMS integration, and audit logs.

[00:39] Carlos (Skybridge): Carlos from procurement, I'll be tracking terms and PO timing.

[00:46] Omar (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. I'll jump in on the technical side. First, quick recap: current Redwood Dedicated footprint is in us-west and us-east for you, and the ask is add EU-edge (Frankfurt) with private VPC peering plus a contract extension to cover an increased baseline. Correct?

[01:05] Liam: Yes, and we're asking for a baseline bump of approx 20% throughput to cover seasonal peaks, with the option to burst. We want autoscaling policies that won't cause throttling for sub-second latencies on routing requests.

[01:20] Maya: Perfect. On the contract side, we can do an amendment for a 12-month extension with the capacity bump and EU-edge add-on as a line item. We'll include canary rollout and performance SLA language — specifically target p95 latency and a throughput SLO. Does that align with what you need, Carlos?

[01:35] Carlos: Yes but we also need explicit termination and price protection clauses — e.g., no surprise uplift during the term.

[01:42] Maya: Understood, we'll add price protection language and an escape clause for failure to meet agreed SLOs.

[01:50] Omar: On the ops plan — for EU edge we offer two deployment paths: 1) Redwood-managed private edge within your VPC using our Private control plane, or 2) a customer-hosted on-prem package with our runtime deployed in your data center. For Skybridge, given compliance and data residency, path 1 with dedicated VPC peering is the recommended sweet spot — you get control plane visibility but we keep runtime in a colocated edge region.

[02:18] Priya: Can you clarify the KMS flow in that setup? We need customer-managed keys, HSM-backed if possible.

[02:25] Omar: Yes — we support customer KMS via external key wrap with HSM integration. For private control plane + peering, keys are stored in your KMS; Redwood references them via configured grants. There's a short handshake; we can provide a sample terraform snippet.

[02:40] Liam: Are audit logs preserved locally? We don't want sensitive PII leaving the VPC.

[02:45] Omar: Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS and we can also keep an audit trail in your account. For high-sensitivity flows, we recommend applying our prefix caching and redaction rules server-side. We'll include those in the runbook.

[02:58] Maya: Quick note — we'll attach the SOC 2 Type II report and our EU data processing addendum in the email after this call.

[03:05] Carlos: Good. Also, procurement likes to see a redline of the MSA with the new terms.

[03:12] Maya: We'll produce a marked-up MSA and the amendment.

[03:18] Priya: On the ops timeline, how long does it take to provision an edge node and get it operational once we give access?

[03:25] Omar: If we do Redwood-managed edge with VPC peering: pre-flight checks 2-3 business days, provisioning and initial tests about 48 hours, then a canary day for load. So end-to-end 7–10 business days if nothing unexpected. If you choose the customer-hosted package, it depends on your infra team but usually 2–3 weeks.

[03:45] Liam: That timing works as long as we start the procurement and the PO by mid-Oct.

[03:52] Maya: Good — we'll target sending the quote and amendment by 2026-10-08.

[03:56] Omar: Now, a quick note on throughput and batching: Skybridge's last-mile use case benefits from small token responses but high QPS. We've recommended a batching window of 15–25 ms with continuous batching disabled for sub-50 ms p99. We'll show a configuration that hits your p95 latency goal but also reduces token unit cost.

[04:18] Priya: We care about p95 more than p99 for user-facing routing right now. p95 under 120 ms is the target.

[04:25] Omar: Okay, we'll aim for p95 <= 120 ms. To hit that we'll use smaller batching and prefer GPU instances with faster attention kernels in the EU edge. We'll include a perf profile.

[04:36] Liam: Any fallback options if the EU edge saturates? We can't have routing refuse requests.

[04:40] Omar: Yes — we have smart routing/fallback to us-west or dedicated fallbacks that maintain correctness. You can set policy: failover to a cheaper model or to hosted model variants in other regions. It will add a latency delta but keep service up. We can also set automatic ramp-down rules to shed non-critical traffic if an overload happens.

[05:00] Maria? (background noise, unclear): [inaudible]

[05:04] Maya: There was some background noise, not sure who that was.

[05:08] Liam: Sorry, that's my laptop.

[05:12] Omar: On security — SSO/SAML support is available, RBAC for token scopes, and audit logs. Priya, you mentioned audit fields earlier, can you list the top 5 you need?

[05:22] Priya: Request ID, user token, model version, region, and payload hash. Also timestamps for KV cache hits/misses.

[05:30] Omar: We'll add those. KV cache metrics are available via our tracing hooks.

[05:35] Maya: Quick procurement question — Carlos, any blockers on your side for a 12-month amendment versus rolling month-to-month?

[05:42] Carlos: Procurement prefers a 12-month commitment for budgeting but we need price protection and a defined SLA otherwise legal will push back. Also need to know the billing cadence and if we can lock in a fixed rate for compute.

[05:55] Maya: We can do monthly invoicing with a committed monthly minimum. We'll include price protection for the 12-month term.

[06:02] Liam: On benchmarks — do you have an existing test harness we can run? We want to run a 48-hour load test simulating peak-hr QPS.

[06:09] Omar: Yes, we have a benchmark harness (we'll share a link) and recommended prompts. For EU edge pilot we'll run a canary with 20% of traffic, observe metrics for 24–48 hours, then increase if stable.

[06:22] Priya: What telemetry will we see in the console? We need token-level cost breakout, per-route latency and per-model KPIs.

[06:30] Omar: All available — console shows token spend by route, p50/95/99 latency, model versions, and traces. We'll enable expanded retention for debug traces for the pilot if you want. Note that longer retention is an add-on.

[06:46] Liam: Can we get a temporary expanded retention for the pilot? That helps validate regressions.

[06:51] Maya: Yes, we can provision extended retention for the pilot window at no extra charge. We'll note that in the quote.

[07:00] Carlos: On the legal side, please include standard indemnification and data processing addendum. We may request some tweaks but start us with your standard redline.

[07:10] Maya: We'll send the marked MSA as requested.

[07:14] Omar: A couple of technical caveats — model quantization choices can reduce cost but may change output character; we'll recommend a quant profile for routing prompts that preserves factuality. Also, continuous KV cache is helpful for repeat prefixes — we can enable prefix caching for routing to reduce token counts.

[07:32] Priya: How do we validate quality degradation risk with quantization in the pilot?

[07:36] Omar: We'll run parallel tests: one with full precision and one with quantized variant and run evals on your prompt set. We'll include regression alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold.

[07:47] Maya: That ties into Redwood Optimize — we can run a quick auto-suggest for quantization settings once we see the initial traces.

[07:55] Liam: Sounds good. A practical question: latency to Frankfurt from our EU POPs — what are typical numbers?

[08:01] Omar: Add ~8–12 ms network plus model inference p95 dependent on model size. With the targeted config, p95 should be under 120 ms as discussed. We'll share empirical numbers from similar customers.

[08:12] Priya: On the topic of failovers, do we get region affinity so sessions stick to EU unless explicitly failing over?

[08:19] Omar: Yes, session affinity with sticky routing is supported; fallback is policy-controlled.

[08:24] Maya: We're approaching the half-hour mark, so maybe we should summarize next steps and owners.

[08:30] Liam: Quick question before summary: If we increase baseline 20% and use burst credits, is there a way to cap burst cost? We need cost predictability.

[08:39] Maya: Yes, we can cap burst spend and set budget alerts. We'll add a burst cap in the pricing sheet and define surge pricing thresholds.

[08:46] Carlos: Good, we prefer a monthly cap with email alerts and an owner escalation.

[08:51] Maya: Ok recap of action items — Omar will share the runbook and network checklist, I'll send updated quote and redlined MSA, Priya will share compliance questions, Carlos to confirm PO timeline. Also schedule the bench test for the week of 10/18. Anything else?

[09:10] Priya: Please include the terraform snippet for KMS grants.

[09:14] Omar: Will do.

[09:17] Liam: Thanks all, excited to get this moving.

[09:20] Maya: Great, we'll follow up via email with links: quote, MSA redline, SOC2 PDF, runbook.

[09:25] Carlos: Expecting that email.

[09:28] Maya: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End transcript.
